title: review (other model): C-O1 notify() portability (T-0078)
spec: Review the diff of T-0078 (branch task/T-0078, worktree wt/T-0078) against its acceptance. Executed by claude:sonnet as the Codex fallback, so this review is on opus. Check: notify() never raises (URL malformed, connection refused, timeout); the webhook body is the message text and the method is POST; osascript is not invoked off darwin and is suppressed by ORCH_NOTIFY_DESKTOP=0; no new dependency; tests are real (they start a local server, not a mock that always passes); README paragraph present and accurate. Verdict approve or request_changes with path:line findings.
acceptance: Each acceptance criterion of T-0078 marked met or not met with evidence

comments.issue: setUp never clears ORCH_NOTIFY_URL, so the new webhook path runs for real whenever the var is exported — which is the documented deployment shape (the daemon autostarts inside the MCP server and inherits that env). Measured: one run of tests.test_daemon makes 11 outbound POSTs, including 'hi" & do shell script "echo pwned' from test_notify_argv_safe and fabricated T-0001/T-0002 merge+hold alerts, to the operator's real alert channel. Against an unreachable-but-not-refusing host it also adds 11x5s to every tests-green gate run. Fix: pop ORCH_NOTIFY_URL/ORCH_NOTIFY_DESKTOP in setUp and let test_webhook_posts_body set it via set_env.

The webhook body is the untruncated msg while the osascript arm two lines below deliberately caps it at msg[:200]. notify() at daemon.py:188 interpolates r.get('reason') from merge stderr, so an arbitrarily large blob of untrusted git output gets POSTed to an external service. Apply the same cap to the body.

urlopen's timeout=5 is per-socket-operation and does not cover getaddrinfo, so a hostname whose resolver hangs blocks notify() for the system DNS timeout. notify() is called synchronously inside tick() at ten call sites (daemon.py:113,143,163,169,186,188,215,230,233,235), several inside per-task loops, so a slow endpoint serialises into the pipeline's hot loop. The spec prescribed this shape, so flagging rather than blocking.

The ORCH_NOTIFY_DESKTOP=0 half of the condition at daemon.py:26 has zero coverage — test_no_osascript_off_darwin only exercises the platform half. One of the two env vars documented in README.md:39 is untested. Not an acceptance failure (the spec named only three tests), but it is the gap.

result.summary: Adversarial review of T-0078 (notify webhook), complexity 4. All four acceptance criteria met and verified by running the suite (90 tests OK; tests.test_daemon 20 OK) and by fuzzing notify() with 8 malformed ORCH_NOTIFY_URL values (never raised). Verdict request_changes on one med defect the criteria did not cover: the new network path fires during the test suite. With ORCH_NOTIFY_URL exported (the documented deployment shape, and the daemon autostarts inside the MCP server inheriting that env), one run of tests.test_daemon makes 11 real outbound POSTs, including the AppleScript injection probe string and fake task IDs, to the operator's alert endpoint. setUp never neutralizes the var; set_env exists but is only ever used to set. Against a blackholed host that also adds 11x5s to the gate. One-line fix in setUp. Criterion-by-criterion evidence: (1) three named tests present at tests/test_daemon.py:261,288,293, all green; (2) never-raises verified empirically across '', 'x', 'http://', '://nope', 'ftp://x/y', 'http://[::1]:1/', 'not a url at all', 'http://999.999.999.999/' plus closed-port; (3) README.md:36-39 documents both vars in one paragraph and flags the ntfy URL as shape only; (4) discover -q tests green, only stdlib urllib.request/http.server added, no dependency change.
